messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a more beautiful open-world Pokémon adventure, adding Johto Pokémon and starters.
- Prefer modern 3D Pokémon models where feasible, with attribution for selected assets.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models; preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining their attribution sidecars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Downloaded Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs with attribution sidecars in `public/models/`.
- Added Johto starter and additional Johto Pokémon entries, plus moves, to `game.js`’s `MOVES` and `DEX`.
- Installed the Sketchfab skill’s npm dependencies and inspected all three GLBs: Chikorita has 4 materials/8 textures, Cyndaquil 2/0, and Totodile 3/3.
- Prepared isolated viewers for all three models; generated a Chikorita viewer screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/chikorita-viewer.png`.

### Active
- Visually verify the downloaded models; only Chikorita’s viewer has been served and screenshotted so far.
- Integrate Johto starters into starter selection and add Johto Pokémon to exploration and battles.
- Load Johto GLBs in `scene3d.js` with procedural fallbacks; enhance the forest and verify the playable game in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the Chikorita viewer screenshot and serve/capture the Cyndaquil and Totodile viewers for visual verification.
2. Finish game integration: starter selection, Johto encounters/rescues, GLB loading, and procedural fallbacks.
3. Improve the exploration environment and run browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Johto roster and moves added; starter selection and exploration still need integration.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment and procedural Pokémon meshes; GLB loading still needed.
- `index.html`: Three.js script setup.
- `style.css`: starter selection styling.
- `public/models/`: Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs and attribution metadata.
- `.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/scripts/prepare_viewer.py`: isolated viewer preparation script.
- `.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs`: GLB inspection script.
- `/tmp/opencode/chikorita-viewer.png`: screenshot from the prepared Chikorita viewer.
- `/tmp/opencode/chikorita-inspection.json`, `/tmp/opencode/cyndaquil-inspection.json`, `/tmp/opencode/totodile-inspection.json`: inspection outputs.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `game.js` is modified and `public/` is untracked.
- Chikorita: UID `8e972a3b516d4789ae621b213116c7a2`, Ramón Ruiz, CC Attribution; `public/models/chikorita.glb` (22,748,632 bytes).
- Cyndaquil: UID `d6aa53b561824ca49295e0c9cd3bb7a2`, Squirmy Worm, CC Attribution; `public/models/cyndaquil.glb` (660,684 bytes).
- Totodile: UID `ca8199356a6a4ad6856045d4ad0a6dad`, A-Z inc., CC Attribution; `public/models/totodile.glb` (449,316 bytes).

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a more beautiful Pokémon adventure, adding Johto Pokémon and starters.
- Prefer 3D Pokémon models where feasible and retain asset attribution.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models; preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining their attribution sidecars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Johto starter and additional Johto Pokémon entries and moves to `game.js`’s `MOVES` and `DEX`.
- Downloaded Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs with attribution sidecars in `public/models/`.
- Inspected all three GLBs; Chikorita has 4 materials/8 textures, Cyndaquil 2/0, and Totodile 3/3.
- Captured isolated Three.js viewer screenshots: `/tmp/opencode/chikorita-viewer.png`, `/tmp/opencode/cyndaquil-viewer.png`, and `/tmp/opencode/totodile-viewer.png`.

### Active
- Integrate Johto starters into starter selection and Johto Pokémon into encounters/rescues.
- Load Johto GLBs in `scene3d.js` with procedural fallbacks; enhance the forest and verify the game in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the captured Cyndaquil and Totodile screenshots and finish evaluating Chikorita’s viewer.
2. Finish game integration: Johto starter selection, Johto encounters/rescues, GLB loading, and procedural fallbacks.
3. Improve the exploration environment and run browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Johto roster and moves are present; starter selection and exploration still need integration.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment and procedural Pokémon meshes; GLB loading still needed.
- `index.html`: Three.js script setup.
- `style.css`: starter selection styling.
- `public/models/`: Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs and attribution metadata.
- `/tmp/opencode/chikorita-viewer.png`: Chikorita viewer screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/cyndaquil-viewer.png`: Cyndaquil viewer screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/totodile-viewer.png`: Totodile viewer screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `game.js` is modified and `public/` is untracked.
- Chikorita: UID `8e972a3b516d4789ae621b213116c7a2`, Ramón Ruiz, CC Attribution; `public/models/chikorita.glb` (22,748,632 bytes).
- Cyndaquil: UID `d6aa53b561824ca49295e0c9cd3bb7a2`, Squirmy Worm, CC Attribution; `public/models/cyndaquil.glb` (660,684 bytes).
- Totodile: UID `ca8199356a6a4ad6856045d4ad0a6dad`, A-Z inc., CC Attribution; `public/models/totodile.glb` (449,316 bytes).

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a more beautiful Pokémon adventure, adding Johto Pokémon and starters.
- Prefer 3D Pokémon models where feasible and retain asset attribution.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models; preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining their attribution sidecars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Johto starter and additional Johto Pokémon entries and moves to `game.js`’s `MOVES` and `DEX`.
- Downloaded Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs with attribution sidecars in `public/models/`.
- Inspected all three GLBs and captured isolated Three.js viewer screenshots in `/tmp/opencode/`.

### Active
- Integrate Johto starters into starter selection and Johto Pokémon into encounters/rescues.
- Load Johto GLBs in `scene3d.js` with procedural fallbacks; enhance the forest and verify the game in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile to the starter selection.
2. Add Johto Pokémon to wild encounters and rescues.
3. Integrate the three GLBs in `scene3d.js`, retaining procedural fallbacks.
4. Improve the exploration environment and run browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Johto roster and moves are present; starter selection and exploration still need integration.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment and procedural Pokémon meshes; GLB loading still needed.
- `index.html`: Three.js and game script setup.
- `style.css`: Starter selection styling.
- `public/models/`: Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs and attribution metadata.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a more beautiful Pokémon adventure, adding Johto Pokémon and starters.
- Prefer 3D Pokémon models where feasible and retain asset attribution.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models; preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining their attribution sidecars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Johto Pokémon entries and moves to `game.js`’s `MOVES` and `DEX`.
- Added all six Kanto and Johto starters to `showStarter()`.
- Downloaded Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs with attribution sidecars in `public/models/`.
- Inspected all three GLBs; they contain no animation clips.

### Active
- Add Johto Pokémon to wild encounters and rescues.
- Integrate the three GLBs in `scene3d.js` with procedural fallbacks.
- Improve the forest environment and verify the game in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add Johto Pokémon to exploration encounters and rescues.
2. Load Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs in `scene3d.js`, retaining procedural fallbacks.
3. Improve the forest environment and run browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Johto roster and moves, six-starter selection; wild encounters still use a Kanto-only list.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment and procedural Pokémon meshes; GLB loading still needed.
- `index.html`: Three.js and game script setup.
- `style.css`: Starter selection styling.
- `public/models/`: Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs and attribution metadata.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `game.js` is modified and `public/` is untracked.
- Chikorita: UID `8e972a3b516d4789ae621b213116c7a2`, Ramón Ruiz, CC Attribution; `public/models/chikorita.glb` (22,748,632 bytes; 4 meshes, 4 materials, 8 textures).
- Cyndaquil: UID `d6aa53b561824ca49295e0c9cd3bb7a2`, Squirmy Worm, CC Attribution; `public/models/cyndaquil.glb` (660,684 bytes; 6 meshes, 2 materials).
- Totodile: UID `ca8199356a6a4ad6856045d4ad0a6dad`, A-Z inc., CC Attribution; `public/models/totodile.glb` (449,316 bytes; 3 meshes, 3 materials, 3 textures; includes skins).

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a more beautiful Pokémon adventure, adding Johto Pokémon and starters.
- Prefer 3D Pokémon models where feasible and retain asset attribution.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models; preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining their attribution sidecars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Johto Pokémon entries and moves to `game.js`’s `MOVES` and `DEX`.
- Added all six Kanto and Johto starters to `showStarter()`.
- Downloaded Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs with attribution sidecars in `public/models/`.
- Inspected all three GLBs; they contain no animation clips.

### Active
- Add Johto Pokémon to wild encounters and rescues.
- Integrate the three GLBs in `scene3d.js` with procedural fallbacks.
- Improve the forest environment and verify the game in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add Johto Pokémon to exploration encounters and rescues.
2. Load Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs in `scene3d.js`, retaining procedural fallbacks.
3. Improve the forest environment and run browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Johto roster and moves, six-starter selection; wild encounters still use a Kanto-only list.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment and procedural Pokémon meshes; GLB loading still needed.
- `index.html`: Three.js and game script setup.
- `style.css`: Starter selection styling.
- `scene3d.css`: Canvas and scene presentation.
- `public/models/`: Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs and attribution metadata.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `game.js` is modified and `public/` is untracked.
- Chikorita: UID `8e972a3b516d4789ae621b213116c7a2`, Ramón Ruiz, CC Attribution; `public/models/chikorita.glb` (22,748,632 bytes; 4 meshes, 4 materials, 8 textures).
- Cyndaquil: UID `d6aa53b561824ca49295e0c9cd3bb7a2`, Squirmy Worm, CC Attribution; `public/models/cyndaquil.glb` (660,684 bytes; 6 meshes, 2 materials).
- Totodile: UID `ca8199356a6a4ad6856045d4ad0a6dad`, A-Z inc., CC Attribution; `public/models/totodile.glb` (449,316 bytes; 3 meshes, 3 materials, 3 textures; includes skins).

## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a richer Pokémon adventure featuring Johto Pokémon and starters, with credited 3D models where feasible and browser verification.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models and preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining attribution sidecars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Johto Pokémon, moves, starter options, and zone-specific encounters and rescue pools in `game.js`.
- Added credited Johto starter GLBs, attribution sidecars, and `public/models/ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- Implemented GLB loading, normalization, procedural fallback, zone palettes, updated scene labels, and post-mission progression into the third zone.
- Verified the game opens in Playwright, renders the 3D scene, offers all six starters, and selecting Cyndaquil displays it in the team. Explored three times; observed mission clues advance to 3/3 and the zone label updates to “Clareira dos Sussurros.”
- `node --check game.js`, `node --check scene3d.js`, and `git diff --check` passed; HTTP checks returned 200 for the page and model.

### Active
- Finish browser verification: test encounters, rescues, boss battle/mission completion, and third-zone progression; check loaded GLB behavior and address any issues.
- Review the full diff and validate attribution and implementation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing from the current session; reach and finish the boss battle and check the resulting zone/model presentation.
2. Exercise encounters and rescues, including Johto rescue eligibility and repeat-rescue prevention.
3. Review changes, rerun syntax/diff checks, and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Pokémon roster, encounters, rescue logic, battles, and zone progression.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment, GLB loading, procedural models, and zone palettes.
- `index.html`: scene labels, import map, and model-credit link.
- `public/models/`: GLBs and attribution sidecars.
- `public/models/ATTRIBUTION.md`: visible credits for selected models.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `game.js`, `index.html`, and `scene3d.js` modified; `public/` untracked.
- Chikorita: Ramón Ruiz, CC BY 4.0; Cyndaquil: Squirmy Worm, CC BY 4.0; Totodile: A-Z inc., CC BY 4.0.
- The development server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright browser opened successfully after installing Chromium. The sole console error was the missing `/favicon.ico` (404); GPU stall warnings occurred during WebGL rendering.
- Current browser state has Cyndaquil selected and the quest at 3/3 clues, in “Clareira dos Sussurros”; `game.js` triggers the boss when quest is complete and exploration count meets the condition.

## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a richer Pokémon adventure featuring Johto Pokémon and starters, with credited 3D models where feasible and browser verification.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models and preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining attribution sidecars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Johto Pokémon, moves, starter options, and zone-specific encounters and rescue pools in `game.js`.
- Added credited Johto starter GLBs, attribution sidecars, and `public/models/ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- Implemented GLB loading, normalization, procedural fallback, zone palettes, updated scene labels, and post-mission progression into the third zone.
- Verified starter selection and scene rendering in Playwright; Cyndaquil appeared in the team and its GLB request returned HTTP 200.
- Verified three clues, boss battle victory, mission completion, Eevee joining the team, save persistence, and progression to “Bosque das Jaulas” / “Rota 03 · Bosque de Johto”.
- `node --check game.js`, `node --check scene3d.js`, and `git diff --check` passed; page and model HTTP checks returned 200.

### Active
- Exercise wild encounters and rescues, including Johto rescue eligibility and repeat-rescue prevention.
- Review the full diff and validate attribution and implementation; confirm browser-visible GLB behavior for all three Johto starters.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test encounters and rescues, including repeat-rescue prevention.
2. Check browser-visible rendering/loading for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile GLBs.
3. Review the full diff and attribution, then rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Pokémon roster, encounters, rescue logic, battles, and zone progression.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment, GLB loading, procedural models, and zone palettes.
- `index.html`: scene labels, import map, and model-credit link.
- `public/models/`: GLBs and attribution sidecars.
- `public/models/ATTRIBUTION.md`: credits for selected models.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `game.js`, `index.html`, and `scene3d.js` modified; `public/` untracked.
- Chikorita: Ramón Ruiz, CC BY 4.0; Cyndaquil: Squirmy Worm, CC BY 4.0; Totodile: A-Z inc., CC BY 4.0.
- Development server is available at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright is open on the game.
- Console reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL GPU stall warnings; model and app requests tested returned 200.

## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a richer Pokémon adventure featuring Johto Pokémon and starters, with credited 3D models where feasible and browser verification.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models and preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining attribution sidecars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Johto Pokémon, moves, starter options, and zone-specific encounters and rescue pools in `game.js`.
- Added credited Johto starter GLBs, attribution sidecars, and `public/models/ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- Implemented GLB loading, normalization, procedural fallback, zone palettes, updated scene labels, and post-mission progression into the third zone.
- Verified starter selection and scene rendering in Playwright; Cyndaquil and Chikorita GLB requests returned HTTP 200.
- Verified clues, boss battle victory, mission completion, Eevee joining the team, save persistence, and progression to “Bosque das Jaulas” / “Rota 03 · Bosque de Johto”.
- Verified Johto rescues: Chikorita and Totodile joined the team; subsequent encounter did not repeat either rescue.
- Confirmed Chikorita visibly rendered in the browser canvas; screenshot saved at `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/output/element-2026-11-12T14-46-25-905Z.png`.
- `node --check game.js`, `node --check scene3d.js`, and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Confirm browser-visible rendering/loading for Totodile’s GLB and review the full diff/asset size.
- Changes remain uncommitted: `game.js`, `index.html`, and `scene3d.js` modified; `public/` untracked.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Switch the active partner to Totodile in Playwright and verify its GLB request and visible rendering.
2. Review the full diff and attribution; check whether asset size is acceptable.
3. Rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Pokémon roster, encounters, rescue logic, battles, and zone progression.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment, GLB loading, procedural models, and zone palettes.
- `index.html`: scene labels, import map, and model-credit link.
- `public/models/`: credited GLBs, attribution sidecars, and model credits.

## Important Context
- Chikorita: Ramón Ruiz, CC BY 4.0; Cyndaquil: Squirmy Worm, CC BY 4.0; Totodile: A-Z inc., CC BY 4.0.
- Development server is available at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright is open on the game.
- Browser checks previously reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL GPU stall warnings; model and app requests tested returned 200.

import io, json, os, struct
from PIL import Image
path = 'public/models/chikorita.glb'
data = open(path, 'rb').read()
if data[:4] != b'glTF': raise SystemExit('Not a GLB file')
version, declared_len = struct.unpack_from('<II', data, 4)
if version != 2 or declared_len != len(data): raise SystemExit('Unexpected GLB version or length')
chunks = []
offset = 12
while offset < len(data):
    length, kind = struct.unpack_from('<II', data, offset)
    chunks.append((kind, data[offset + 8:offset + 8 + length]))
    offset += 8 + length
json_chunk = next(payload for kind, payload in chunks if kind == 0x4E4F534A)
bin_chunk = next(payload for kind, payload in chunks if kind == 0x004E4942)
gltf = json.loads(json_chunk)
replacements = {}
for image in gltf.get('images', []):
    view_index = image.get('bufferView')
    if view_index is None:
        continue
    view = gltf['bufferViews'][view_index]
    start = view.get('byteOffset', 0)
    raw = bin_chunk[start:start + view['byteLength']]
    texture = Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw)).convert('RGB')
    texture.thumbnail((1024, 1024), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    output = io.BytesIO()
    if 'basecolor' in image.get('name', '').lower() or 'base_color' in image.get('name', '').lower():
        texture.save(output, format='JPEG', quality=86, optimize=True)
        image['mimeType'] = 'image/jpeg'
    else:
        texture.save(output, format='PNG', optimize=True)
        image['mimeType'] = 'image/png'
    replacements[view_index] = output.getvalue()
# Rebuild in source order, preserving every referenced buffer view and 4-byte alignment.
views = gltf['bufferViews']
spans = sorted((v.get('byteOffset', 0), v.get('byteOffset', 0) + v['byteLength'], i) for i, v in enumerate(views))
for left, right in zip(spans, spans[1:]):
    if left[1] > right[0]: raise SystemExit(f'Overlapping buffer views: {left} / {right}')
new_binary = bytearray()
for start, end, index in spans:
    while len(new_binary) % 4:
        new_binary.append(0)
    view = views[index]
    view['byteOffset'] = len(new_binary)
    payload = replacements.get(index, bin_chunk[start:end])
    view['byteLength'] = len(payload)
    new_binary.extend(payload)
while len(new_binary) % 4:
    new_binary.append(0)
gltf['buffers'][0]['byteLength'] = len(new_binary)
new_json = json.dumps(gltf, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')
new_json += b' ' * ((-len(new_json)) % 4)
new_bin = bytes(new_binary)
new_glb = b'glTF' + struct.pack('<II', 2, 12 + 8 + len(new_json) + 8 + len(new_bin))
new_glb += struct.pack('<II', len(new_json), 0x4E4F534A) + new_json
new_glb += struct.pack('<II', len(new_bin), 0x004E4942) + new_bin
open(path, 'wb').write(new_glb)
sidecar_path = path + '.attribution.json'
sidecar = json.load(open(sidecar_path))
sidecar['sourceGlbBytes'] = sidecar.pop('glbBytes', len(data))
sidecar['glbBytes'] = len(new_glb)
sidecar['optimization'] = 'Base-color textures resized to max 1024px and JPEG quality 86; other textures resized to max 1024px and optimized as PNG.'
open(sidecar_path, 'w').write(json.dumps(sidecar, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\n')
print(f'Optimized Chikorita GLB: {len(data):,} -> {len(new_glb):,} bytes ({100 * len(new_glb) / len(data):.1f}%)')

Core:

## Objective
- Expand “PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta” into a richer Pokémon adventure featuring Johto Pokémon and starters, with credited 3D models where feasible and browser verification.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing Portuguese game without asking clarifying questions.
- Add Johto starters and Pokémon beyond Kanto.
- Prefer 3D models and preserve attribution for selected assets.

## Decisions
- Keep procedural Pokémon meshes as fallbacks if GLB loading fails.
- Use credited Sketchfab models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, retaining attribution sidecars.
- Optimize Chikorita’s embedded textures rather than replace the model.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Johto Pokémon, moves, starter options, and zone-specific encounters and rescue pools in `game.js`.
- Added credited Johto starter GLBs, attribution sidecars, and `public/models/ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- Implemented GLB loading, normalization, procedural fallback, zone palettes, updated scene labels, and post-mission progression into the third zone.
- Reduced `public/models/chikorita.glb` from 22,748,632 bytes to 1,613,100 bytes by resizing textures to 1024px and recompressing them; updated its attribution sidecar with optimization and source-size details.
- Verified Chikorita GLB structure and embedded images, and confirmed its HTTP 200 response and browser rendering; Cyndaquil and Totodile also returned HTTP 200.
- Previously verified starter selection, scene rendering, clues, boss victory, mission completion, Eevee joining, save persistence, zone progression, and Johto Pokémon rescues in Playwright.
- `node --check game.js`, `node --check scene3d.js`, and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Changes remain uncommitted: `game.js`, `index.html`, and `scene3d.js` modified; `public/` untracked.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Pokémon roster, encounters, rescue logic, battles, and zone progression.
- `scene3d.js`: Three.js environment, GLB loading, procedural models, and zone palettes.
- `index.html`: scene labels, import map, and model-credit link.
- `public/models/`: credited GLBs, attribution sidecars, and model credits.

## Important Context
- Chikorita: Ramón Ruiz; Cyndaquil: Squirmy Worm; Totodile: A-Z inc.; all models are CC BY 4.0.
- Development server is available at `http://localhost:3002`; browser verification is available.

Expanded **PokéRamPaGe — Crônicas da Floresta** with Johto starters and Pokémon, new moves and encounters, and progression into a third zone. Added credited 3D models for Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile, with procedural fallbacks and attribution credits.

Optimized Chikorita’s model from **22.7 MB to 1.6 MB** while preserving its geometry and materials. Verified the model loads in the browser, and `node --check` and `git diff --check` pass.

The changes are present in the working tree and remain uncommitted.
